Subject: SLA rollback trigger + seasonal peak capacity discount — clarification

Hi Kate — great to be moving this forward. Two items came up in your procurement note and I wanted to confirm our position so we can get a clean redline back to you:

1) SLA rollback trigger: you asked for clarity on the "rollback" mechanism when we can’t meet an uptime band. Our standard is an availability metric measured monthly; the rollback clause you saw is intended as a temporary automatic downgrade to the next availability tier when outages exceed 0.5% for more than two consecutive 24-hour windows. Practically, that means we automatically switch to the fallback tier (and cap credits accordingly) while we deploy remediation. We log each rollback with timestamps and remediation notes in the audit trail.

2) Peak capacity discount: you mentioned predictable seasonality for Q4 spikes. We can offer a peak-capacity addendum where Stratus purchases burst credits (pre-bought token pool) at a discounted rate and those credits apply only during declared peak windows. We also offer an alternate structure — a committed flexible baseline with an overage discount once you breach a monthly committed token threshold.

I attached a short term-sheet summarizing both mechanics (SLA_rollback_term_sheet.pdf) and an example pricing tab (peak_capacity_pricing_sheet.xlsx). Can you confirm the procurement timeline and whether legal needs a one-page vs full contract for initial sign-off? If procurement wants a single consolidated clause we can prepare a 1-page redline.

Next steps I suggest:
- You confirm procurement preferred format by EOD Wed (9/8)
- If helpful, we can schedule a 30-min call this week to walk the rollback event flow and how credits calculate.

Thanks,
Jonas
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Thanks Kate — quick clarifications inline:

- Audit trail export: yes — rollback events are recorded in our control plane and we expose an export endpoint (CSV) and a Drive-style link for each event. We'll include the exact export sample in the 1-pager.

- Credits formula (plain language): the spreadsheet example shows two parallel mechanisms —
  a) Automatic rollback credit: when monthly availability drops below the SLA threshold for the committed tier, we calculate a pro-rated credit based on the percentage shortfall of available minutes vs promised minutes across the month, capped at the maximum credit for that tier. (Example: Tier A promises 99.9% -> 43.2 minutes allowable downtime per month; if downtime measures 120 minutes, shortfall % = (120 - 43.2)/ (total minutes in month) -> credit = shortfall% * monthly invoice amount, capped at the tier cap.)
  b) Peak capacity pre-bought credits: you can buy a pool of burst credits at a 15% discount vs on-demand. During declared peak windows, usages draw from the pool first; if pool exhausted, overages are billed with an agreed overage discount table (5–10% depending on volume).

What I'll do now: produce the one-page summary that contains (1) the rollback flow diagram, (2) a CSV export sample, and (3) the credit math in plain language with the worked example from the spreadsheet. Expect that by EOD.

If procurement confirms the 9/15 decision target, we'll also prepare a DocuSign-ready one-pager so legal can sign off quickly.

Regards,
Jonas
